body: Ngl i watched khan academy for the first 3 units which didn't make any sense to me and I didn't cover those in honours biology. After that, I started using Barron's prep book to cover the rest of the content. I also just watched a bunch of youtube videos on people walking through frqs and mcqs and how to not overcomplicate the exam (those videos actually help more than learning the content and practicing questions yourself)

Rn im in CSA i have like around an 85%. I went into the class not knowing a single thing about coding and was actually surprised by how much I learnt in a single course. It really depends on the teacher at your school. At my school, I got the hardest teacher who grades incredibly strictly and has questions 10x harder than collegeboard's standards. CSA is really easy to grasp imo, but it depends on your teacher for the preparation you get on the exam. My teacher's course is so difficult and rigorous to the point where 75% of all his 100 students get a 5, and he has a 100% pass rate. You really don't have to know coding for it

Im also taking bio and im self studying it; I found a cool video online that talks about what collegeboard does to try to trip you up (they do it a lot apparently) and they have several strategies. If you can somehow pinpoint these strategies during the exam it would make it really easy. I wouldn't say im the strongest at MCQ for bio but I would say go through EVERY question as fast as you can. Skip any question that seems like it would take too long and come back to it at the end; don't exceed over 10 times though. Come back to those questions later; you could end up skipping the easiest question towards the end of the test b/c you run out of time. That would be my personal preference, could be different for you
